units.en: Each country has one of the four ⟦0⟧ (usually referred to as ⟦1⟧). These are difficult to change and affect under what circumstances a country can perform certain actions, and what happens to occupied territory.

Ideology types (usually referred to as sub-ideologies) have only a modest impact on the game: interacting with the alt-history focuses of several nations (Communist Italy, Right Opposition USSR, and Fascist Poland all have focuses that distinguish between the Marxist and Stalinist sub-ideologies of Communism, the Rexist sub-idology of Fascism, and the Democratic Socialism sub-ideology of Democracy; for instance) but have almost no impact on historical paths.

The main effect sub-ideologies have in the base game is that countries with the same ideology subtype gain the ⟦0⟧ ( ⟦1⟧ opinion) opinion modifier toward each other, while countries with the same ideology group yet different sub-ideologies gain the ⟦2⟧ ( ⟦3⟧ opinion) opinion modifier toward each other.

The name and the description of the ideology type shows up when hovering over the ideology icon in the country's politics or diplomacy view. In case of the anarchism ideology within the non-aligned group, a different icon is also used.
Democracy is a form of government in which the popular vote governs, directly or indirectly. It is characterized by a commitment to civil liberties.
⟦0⟧: Considering rapid changes to society to be potentially harmful, conservatism espouses tradition and moderate reforms, sometimes advocating a return to old moral values.
⟦0⟧: With a long philosophical tradition of valuing personal liberty, liberalism views safeguarding these rights as the primary function of the state.
⟦0⟧: Striving for equality and a socialist state by reformist means, democratic socialism aims to abolish or mitigate the effects of capitalism with public mandate.

⟦0⟧: A political movement with little clear ideological framework. Populists advocate for policies from across the spectrum that are popular with the electorate or are perceived as at odds with the preferences of the political 'elite.'
Can declare war on country with the same ideology group without a war goal
Cannot justify war goals against countries that have not generated ⟦0⟧
Can force government of another country to adopt the same ideology
Democracies cannot occupy territory owned by neutral countries, it is given to the owner instead.

Impact of war declaration on World Tension: ⟦0⟧
Impact of joining faction on World Tension: ⟦0⟧
Change ideology on Fascist country cost ⟦0⟧
Change ideology on Communist country cost ⟦0⟧
Countries that start out as a democracy
Communism is a form of government based on social equality and collective ownership of the means of production.

⟦0⟧: Encompassing a broad spectrum of economic and historical views, Marxist politics seek to apply the theories of Karl Marx to political practice. Class struggle and the need for transition to a society based on common ownership of the means of production characterize these ideologies.

⟦0⟧: A political ideology based in Marxist thought, Leninism seeks to establish a socialist state by a vanguard party leading a revolution overthrowing capitalist society. Once in power, the party rules through a system whereby policies are open for internal debate until a decision has been made.

⟦0⟧: Identifying as a form of government applying and developing Marxist-Leninist policies, Stalinism emphasizes rapid industrialization and collectivization as well as the need for a strong authoritative socialist state to purge any counter-revolutionary elements.

⟦0⟧: A reaction to the many ideologies claiming to be successors to Marxism, Anti-Revisionism advocates retaining key elements of original revolutionary theory. Mainly opposing incorporation of capitalist economic elements into socialist states, the ideology is defined as much by what it isn't as what it is.

⟦0⟧: An ideology embracing the idea of communism as a stateless society, Anarchist Communism eschews the idea of a transitionary socialist state and favors a society based on voluntary associations and mutual aid.

⟦0⟧: Buddhist socialism, also referred to as Dhammic or Natural socialism, is a political ideology which advocates socialism based on the principles of Buddhism. Both Buddhism and socialism seek to provide an end to suffering by analyzing its conditions and removing its main causes through praxis. Both also seek to provide a transformation of personal consciousness to bring an end to human alienation and selfishness.
World Tension required to join faction: ⟦0⟧
Countries that start out as communist
Fascism is a form of government characterized by authoritarian nationalism.

⟦0⟧: Rooted in extreme nationalism, National Socialism is driven by ideas of Germanic supremacy. It promotes aggressive expansionism and a totalitarian state where the people are united under a leader with absolute power, the Führer.

⟦0⟧: Rooted in extreme nationalism, National Socialism is driven by ideas of racial supremacy. It promotes aggressive expansionism and a totalitarian state where the people are united under a leader with absolute power.
⟦0⟧: Encompassing a variety of ultra-nationalist movements, fascism typically venerates devotion to the state and uniting the people under a strong leader.
⟦0⟧: An authoritarian ideology with traits of fascism and conservatism, Falangism values national and Catholic identity.

⟦0⟧: Strongly opposed to both liberal and communist ideals, Rexism is a staunchly conservative nationalist movement who advocate a corporatist economic policy. Employing increasingly populist and authoritarian rhetoric, their ideals are shifting closer to other fascist movements.

⟦0⟧: Emperor Fascism is a form of Ultranationalism in which the masses do not hold a say, often referred to as 'fascism from above', where the rule is held by the military and aristocratic bureaucrats, with great reverence for the nations emperor, a monarch who is regarded as an infallible divine figure.
Is also called "Nazism" in-game, but "gen_nazism" in the localization files.
Time to justify war when at war with major power: ⟦0⟧
World Tension requirement to join faction: ⟦0⟧
Countries that start out as fascist
The term "Non-Aligned" is used to describe any remaining ideology that does not align with the other three categories.
⟦0⟧: Despotism is a form of government in which a single person rules with absolute power.
⟦0⟧: An oligarchy is a form of government in which a small group of individuals holds absolute power.
⟦0⟧: Moderatism is a form of government which avoids the extremes of left and right by taking a moderate position or course of action.

⟦0⟧: Centrism is a form of government which wants to achieve common sense solutions that appropriately address current and future needs, that support the public trust and serve the common good with consideration of risk and capacity in context of these needs.
⟦0⟧: Anarchism is the rejection of authority itself, promoting the division of society into self-managing and self-governing collectives instead of a singular, centralized state.

⟦0⟧: Militarism is an ideology in which the leader of the nation holds only nominal control, and acts more like a puppet to the nation's military than an independent politician, constantly forwarding their agenda with the end goal of rapid expansionist policy.
Can impose its ideology on other countries
Impact of declaring war on World Tension: ⟦0⟧
Impact of joining factions on World Tension: ⟦0⟧
A country can change its ideology in four ways:
Having an election while another ideology has more than 50% support. This creates an event that enables a peaceful change of power without a civil war.
Fighting and winning a civil war. The support of the conflicting ideology decides how much troops and states they get at the beginning.
